blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why some people remain jobless even when jobs seem available? Let's explore the complexities of unemployment and labour.

blocks.markdown: In economics, understanding the labour force and unemployment is crucial. The labour force includes all individuals who are willing and able to work, both employed and unemployed. Unemployment occurs when people who are willing and able to work cannot find jobs.

blocks.title: Labour Force and Unemployment
blocks.text: The labour force consists of individuals aged 15 and above who are either employed or actively seeking employment. Unemployment refers to the situation where people are willing and able to work but cannot find jobs.

blocks.markdown: There are various types of unemployment, each with distinct causes and characteristics. Understanding these types helps in formulating policies to reduce unemployment.

items: Frictional Unemployment: Short-term unemployment during transitions between jobs.
Structural Unemployment: Caused by changes in the economy that eliminate certain jobs.
Seasonal Unemployment: Occurs in industries that operate only during certain seasons.
Cyclical Unemployment: Results from economic recessions.
Residual Unemployment: Due to personal factors such as disabilities or lack of skills.

blocks.title: Understanding Unemployment Types
blocks.prompt: Identify the type of unemployment in the following scenario: A farmer in Jos is unemployed during the dry season.

steps.text: Identify the industry: Agriculture, which is seasonal.
Determine the nature of unemployment: The farmer is unemployed due to seasonal changes.

blocks.markdown: Wages are determined by various factors including the skill level of workers, demand and supply of labour, and government regulations. Understanding these factors helps in comprehending how wages are set in the labour market.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When distinguishing types of unemployment, focus on the cause and duration of unemployment to accurately identify the type.

points: The labour force includes all individuals who are willing and able to work.
Unemployment can be categorized into frictional, structural, seasonal, cyclical, and residual types.
Wages are influenced by factors such as skill level, demand and supply, and government policies.
